highlights.title: Kitchen Composters I Recommend After 2 Years of Testing (2026)
highlights.summary: After enduring years of smells, strange noises, and waste “tea,” I’ve found the composters and food recyclers I’d actually recommend.
body: The countertop kitchen composter is a lovely thought. Instead of a smelly bucket of vegetable scraps and coffee grounds breeding fruit flies on your counter or attracting rats to your backyard, you could just put it all into a nifty electric gadget, and at some undetermined point in the future you'll have a bountiful supply of nutrient-rich compost to use in your garden.

Unfortunately, none of the more popular electric kitchen composters do exactly this. Even though some of these devices are marketed as “composters” and have instruction booklets and apps detailing all the ways in which one can use compost, the vast majority of kitchen composters are just going to grind up and dry your food scraps. You will greatly reduce your food waste output, and it will no longer smell, but if you’re hoping to put eggshells and banana peels into a machine and magically scoop out the kind of compost you’d buy at the garden center, that’s just not going to happen.

highlights.title: I watched a humanoid robot clean my apartment. It felt like a taste of the future.
highlights.summary: I’m not the sort of person who typically pays for a house cleaner. I’m too frugal, and I kind of enjoy putting on a podcast and going to town on my tub with a Magic Eraser. But when I saw an X post about a new humanoid-robot cleaning service in San Francisco, I immediately signed…
body: Because this data is so valuable to Tau, the company charges less for cleaning than one might expect for such a cutting-edge product. At the time I booked, Tau was offering $30 for an hourlong cleaning with a single robot; now the charge is $60 per weekly cleaning with two robots, or $100 for a one-time visit. But even at the cheaper rate of $30 per hour, Tau’s robots aren’t a great bargain. They are thorough but slow, so if you, like me, are tempted to stand around watching them for their entire visit, it would probably be a better use of your time to just take care of the cleaning yourself.

But the robots are physically capable of cleaning, and they’re undeniably cute. Tau has armed each four-and-a-half-foot-tall robot with a 3D-printed “head” with antennae that allow it to communicate with Tau’s headquarters, as well as two 3D-printed claw “hands” (the more humanlike alternatives apparently aren’t durable enough, and claws do surprisingly well for most cleaning tasks). Mine was wearing a Tau Robotics shirt, and grippy socks so that it didn’t scratch hardwood floors.

highlights.title: It's Official: The PlayStation Blackout Protest Did Nothing
highlights.summary: Disgruntled players tried to boycott Sony in August after the company announced it would discontinue physical media. However, it seems that the PlayStation Digital Blackout protest was a bust.
body: With Sony ceasing disc production in January 2028 and allegedly trying to establish a digital game monopoly, PlayStation owners who were unhappy with its recent business practices organized a boycott. From Aug. 23 until Aug. 30, participants pledged not to make in-game purchases, buy digital games, or renew PlayStation Plus subscriptions. However, the protest gained less traction than expected. Circana's video game industry advisor, Mat Piscatella, initially noted that there hadn't been any significant change in player count or engagement during the blackout.

The financial records have confirmed the protest's insignificance to Sony's business. Not only did sales and engagement not go down, but they actually went up, with Insomniac Games' Marvel's Wolverine leading the charge with 2.4 million units sold. Compared to the previous quarter, monthly active users increased by 2 million and digital sales rose by ¥138.8 billion — ¥158.7 billion if you count add-ons, which is about $996.2 million, using FYQ2's average conversion rate.

highlights.title: Global stocks plunge as fears over US AI slowdown spread to Asia and Europe
highlights.summary: Investors have reacted to possible tougher scrutiny of data centre construction and the AI industry.
body: Global stock markets have tumbled after investors sold tech shares on fears that the US midterm elections would slow the development of artificial intelligence (AI).
The sell-off, which started in the US and then spread to Asia and Europe, has seen trillions of dollars wiped off the stock value of major tech firms.
In the US, the tech-heavy Nasdaq share index sank 5.5% on Thursday. Asian markets also saw hefty falls on Friday and European markets opened lower.

Investors are worried about tougher regulation of AI, after Democrat candidates opposed the data centres needed by the technology. The share falls also come on top of concerns about whether the huge amounts being spent on AI will pay off.

highlights.summary: The coach who helped guide Jannik Sinner to five Grand Slam titles and the world number one spot is to leave the player's camp at the end of the year.
body: Australian Darren Cahill, 61, joined the Italian's team in June 2022 when Sinner was just outside the world's top 10 and had never progressed beyond the quarter-finals of a Grand Slam tournament.
But, together with Italian coach Simone Vagnozzi, Cahill has helped Sinner to go on to win five Slams and occupy the world number one spot for 95 weeks.
Injury has meant the 25-year-old has not played since winning Wimbledon for the second year in a row in July, which led to Alexander Zverev recently overtaking him at the top of the rankings.
He is set to return to action at the Six Kings Slam tournament in Saudi Arabia next month.

highlights.title: Nier: Automata Dev Working on Fix for Patch That Accidentally Bloated the Game Size to 366GB on PC
highlights.summary: Nier: Automata got a patch yesterday to add support for more languages to the game (Korean, Simplified Chinese, and Traditional Chinese), but it accidentally bloated the game file size to 366GB on PC. That’s 1.5 copies of GTA 6!
body: A bug caused the entire game to be applied to every DLC pack included in the PC edition, ballooning the overall file size to Call of Duty-esque heights. Nier was previously around 50GB to download.
The game saw a wave of negative reviews come in on Steam following the patch, with players complaining that they were unable to play or, you know, download any other games.

"Claude, please add new language support for my game, no mistakes, masterpiece. It's 366 gigabytes now? Splendid,” said one review, making a joke about Square Enix using AI. “Undeniably good game which I've had to remove from my computer because some genius, presumably misusing automated tools, packed it into itself six times over, making a 360 gig install file. I'll recommend this game after it is fixed,” said another.

“I think the funniest part about the ‘slight’ issue with the new update for language support is the Steam page still lists a 50gb storage requirement. Good one guys,” reads another negative review. “Played this on PS4 loved it but 366GB is unacceptable for a company like them... fix this Square or I will STOP my FF14 sub,” read another.

highlights.summary: UN conference this month seen as key moment after years of discussions on filling gap in governance of AI systems. Plans to fill a gap in the global governance of autonomous weapons are in jeopardy as a group of nations led by Russia and the US move to use a UN conference this month to block…
body: The scale of the opposition will become clear at a diplomatic retreat starting on Friday before the seventh review conference on “certain conventional weapons” in Geneva due to be attended by 128 countries from 16 to 20 November.

The review conference is seen as the key moment when the world could decide whether to back a mandate to negotiate a legally binding instrument negotiated within a defined timetable. The speed with which autonomous weapons are being developed and used in warfare is widely acknowledged.

Anna Hehir, the head of military AI governance at the Future of Life Institute, an independent nonprofit, said: “States have never been closer to launching a global agreement on AI weapons. A lot of the hard work has already been done and states have now agreed by consensus to elements of a draft treaty text that would be the basis for negotiations to start.

highlights.title: OpenAI is stepping back from NDAs for data center projects
highlights.summary: Following this week's midterms where voters resoundingly voiced their opposition to data center expansion, OpenAI today announced new commitments to communities where it is working on data center projects, including that it won't use non-disclosure agreements (NDAs) with public officials.
body: The ChatGPT maker won’t use NDAs with public officials as part of its new data center community commitments.

Many data center projects have come under scrutiny for relying on NDAs to hide discussions between developers and local officials. However, OpenAI says it is now allowing “only narrow protections covering legitimate security information, trade secrets, or proprietary or competitively sensitive information.” In October, Amazon announced it would no longer use NDAs with government agencies it works with on data center projects.

OpenAI’s additional commitments include paying “the full cost” of electricity it uses and the “infrastructure needed to serve us.” It will make opportunities for local communities by publishing the jobs it expects to create and by reporting on hiring. And every future “compute campus” (its rebranding phrase for data centers ) the company owns and operates will have a “local compact” that includes the commitments and will reflect “local priorities,” OpenAI says.

highlights.title: Zelda: Ocarina of Time Producer Doesn’t Want Nintendo’s Next Generation To Rely on BotW’s Ideas
highlights.summary: Nintendo’s Legend of Zelda series has remained relevant for 40 years, a streak that the Switch 2’s new Ocarina of Time remake is already set to continue. If you’re looking to understand how a game series stays fresh for four decades, part of that answer can be found in the series’ constant…
body: In an interview with Polygon, producer Hidemaro Fujibayashi explained why Zelda games tend to change rather than stick to one formula. For the series’ producers, a lot of it comes down to the creative freedom that gives the series a natural "malleability," according to Fujibayashi.

That philosophy is currently top of mind for Fujibayashi as the Zelda series enters a new era. For Ocarina of Time, the series’ long-time producers worked with many fresh developers, some of whom weren’t very familiar with the original game. When working with those developers, Fujibayashi said that he encourages the team not to simply take notes from previous games.

“A lot of times, the question I have when I talk to younger staff is like, ‘Is that going to be fun?’” Fujibayashi said. “Or I would say sometimes, ‘Well, I think we did that in Breath of the Wild. I think we touched that on Tears of Kingdom. I feel like I saw it in Ocarina of Time.’ These are just examples, I don't actually directly say that. But this is the kind of probing and discussion that we do with the team such that they don't feel like they need to pull from an already existing pool of ideas that Zelda has plotted.”

highlights.title: Perplexity launches its own take on AI agents for work
highlights.summary: Perplexity is taking on OpenAI and Anthropic with its own work-focused AI agents. The startup's new always-on "Teammates" can take on multiple roles within a workspace, while pulling existing projects, skills, and memory from the Perplexity tools you already use.
body: Like OpenAI’s Dots and Claude Duet, Perplexity’s Teammates can perform an array of tasks while running 24/7.

Teammates integrate with Perplexity Computer, an AI system that can deploy agents on your device to complete tasks. But Perplexity says Teammates “build on top” of Computer by offering the ability to collaborate and complete “ongoing, large-scale work.” You can assign each Teammate different jobs that they can perform simultaneously — much like OpenAI’s Dots and Claude Duet. Perplexity’s take on the feature is much more expensive, however, as it requires a subscription to its $200 / month Max plan.

Perplexity notes that you can keep tabs on Teammates’ progress through individual threads in the Perplexity app, as well as interact with them in Slack. “Over time, we envision every org having hundreds of teammates working for each person,” Perplexity CEO Aravind Srinivas says on X.

body: MLR was formed in 2018, and by 2022 the competition supported 13 teams. In 2025, teams in Utah, Miami, Los Angeles, Houston and New Orleans dropped out.

The league went ahead in 2026 with just six teams but Anthem RC, a World Rugby backed project in Charlotte, North Carolina, will not return next year. Seattle Seawolves, champions in 2018 and 2019, are the only founding members remaining. The other teams are Chicago Hounds, New England Free Jacks, Old Glory DC and California Legion.

MLR co-president Alex Magleby, a former US Eagles flanker and coach, told the Guardian the league hoped six of the 17 groups in talks to host a team would enter a formal bid process ahead of the 2028 season, with three to be selected.

Magleby described a “disciplined, milestone-driven expansion framework,” with candidates advancing “through distinct vetting gates: initial milestone review under a Letter of Intent (LOI), an Exclusive Negotiating Agreement (ENA), and final Board approval before a definitive Franchise Agreement is awarded”.

highlights.title: Can a Radar-Equipped AC Actually Cut Your Power Bill?
highlights.summary: Air conditioners can now follow you from room to room to cut power draw. Saving the planet, however, won’t come from a smarter breeze.
body: With rolling heat waves sweeping the globe, 2027 is shaping up to be the hottest year on record. As the health risks of extreme temperatures mount, there's never been a better time to rethink sustainable cooling.

Air conditioners and electric fans account for around 20 percent of electricity used in buildings worldwide— 3 to 4 percent of total greenhouse gas emissions—and, as demand for cooling in homes, workplaces, and schools grows, the number of AC units in use could reach 5.5 billion by 2050.

The solution isn't one magic fix, but a suite of emerging technologies heading for living rooms and apartment windows. From radar sensors tracking your body to compact heat pumps and climate-safe refrigerants, here is how the next generation of air-conditioning plans to keep us cool without cooking the planet.

In 1994, Mitsubishi Electric was zooming past the air-con competition, introducing the first motion and occupancy sensors for AC, with infrared 3D sensing eventually following in the mid-2010s. Fast-forward to 2026 and AI-powered ACs now track people in the home with millimeter-level precision.

There was not huge optimism at the start of the season when Everton sold Iliman Ndiaye and were unable to make the signings they had hoped for late in the transfer window. "We had a difficult summer," concedes Moyes. But it has been a better autumn.

"I think the players have done a great job in getting ourselves into this position." But how about some credit for the manager too? Everton were at a low ebb when he took over last year, but Moyes has more than stabilised, raising the standards at the club again.

Next month, in his second spell alone, he will become Everton's longest-serving manager since Roberto Martinez - the man who first replaced him over 13 years ago. But there is a bigger landmark that he will reach at the Hill Dickinson Stadium on Friday.

The company’s recent IPO filing didn’t even mention the possibility of selling ads to make money from the AI chatbot. It’s easy to maintain the high ground with about $112 billion in investor cash.

The chatbot industry, though, may find selling ads necessary to defray the high costs of generating AI responses. OpenAI is all in, with over 100,000 customers advertising in ChatGPT since ads debuted there in February. Last week, Google expanded ads in its search chatbot AI Mode to 10 more countries beyond the US and declared that users “find them highly relevant.” Advertisers are far from satisfied with the experience, but they expect it to improve.

highlights.summary: It's only been two weeks since we last heard Warren Spector sound off about EA's sudden decision to close BioWare, following the publisher's acquisition by Saudi Arabia's PIF and venture capitalist concerns. But now, the storied developer is back and - apparently - angrier than ever.
body: "I recently posted my thoughts about EA’s shuttering of BioWare," Spector wrote in a post on LinkedIn. "Those of you who read my post know that I was unhappy. I remain so. The tragedy of so many layoffs the last few years hasn’t been lost on me, but for some reason, BioWare hit me on an emotional level that nothing before had. I felt gut-punched."

Spector goes on to counter the idea that the studio was closed down as a "sound business decision" because the "studio’s glory days (artistic and commercial) were behind them" and that "businesses don’t succeed on history alone". These reactions, more than anything else, appear to be what's inspired Spector to take to posting again - he simply cannot agree with this assessment.

"If studio-level people leave, resulting in dilution of talent, someone is creating an environment that pushes them out. Do those culture-killers pay any price? If executives misread the market, over-hire, or make decisions that result in under-funded, over-funded, poorly-marketed games do they lose sleep let alone jobs?" he asks.

highlights.title: Rocky review – 50 years on Stallone’s boxer remains a gritty contender
highlights.summary: The actor’s triumphant breakthrough has clear ancestors in grimy tales of working-class struggle, but finds a fresh, rousing idealism. Peter Farrelly’s new film I Play Rocky is about the underdog-with-heart story of how a great boxing movie got made against the odds with its plucky young untried…
body: Rocky thoughtfully tells Adrian how tough boxing is, how loaded it is against fighters like him, and how it is almost designed to turn boxers into wrecks. When a movie audience hears that Rocky has been promised $150,000 as his share of the purse, they must wince with anticipation at the betrayal that is surely coming. He’s going to get cheated of that fortune … isn’t he? Similarly, when the loathsome Gazzo gives Rocky $500 for training expenses, we wince again. Rocky is now in debt to this gangster. Gazzo is going to demand some sort of quid quo pro. Will Rocky be asked to take a dive?

The answer in both cases, by a kind of miracle, is no. (Or at least we can assume that the answer to the first is no, and definitely no to the second.) Rocky is a film that appears to remember the melancholy destiny of Brando in On the Waterfront and also the ugly racial contest in something like The Great White Hope, which starred James Earl Jones as the Jim Crow-era black boxer Jack Johnson. But it turns despair on its head.

highlights.title: Benjamina Ebuehi’s recipe for steamed chocolate puddings with malted chocolate sauce | The sweet spot
highlights.summary: It’s steamed pudding season again, and there are few better ways to serve it than with hot chocolate sauce and a scoop of ice-cream. This is the best time of the year for proper stodge, and an even better time to make steamed puddings.
body: Grease seven small pudding basins (of about 170-190ml capacity) with butter and cut out a small round of baking paper to fit in the bases.

Put the butter and sugar in a bowl and beat for two to three minutes, until smooth and creamy. Whisk in the eggs one at a time, then sift in the flour, cocoa powder, baking powder and salt, stirring just until the mix comes together and there are no pockets of flour hiding in the bottom of the bowl. Stir in the milk, then divide the batter evenly between the greased and lined basins.

Put seven small sheets of foil on top of seven pieces of baking paper, make a pleat in the middle of each, then put them paper side down on top of each pudding basin. Scrunch the edges to hold the lids in place.

Put a wide pan on the hob and put a steaming tray or upturned plate inside. Add the pudding basins and fill with enough hot water to come about halfway up the sides of the puddings. Cover and leave to steam for 40-45 minutes, until the puddings feel firm to the touch. Unwrap and turn out on to plates.

highlights.title: Cult.fit builds operational muscle with Codex
highlights.summary: Cult.fit is using Codex to help teams across functions build tools, move faster, and change how work gets done.
body: Cult.fit is one of India’s leading technology-enabled fitness companies, operating 708 fitness centers across 77 cities and serving nearly one million paid members. Its business combines subscription-based access to gyms and trainer-led fitness classes with a growing consumer products portfolio spanning fitness equipment, accessories, workout footwear and activewear.

As the company grew, it wanted to solve more operational and product challenges without adding layers of process and complexity. By standardizing engineering on Codex and then extending it beyond engineering, cult.fit is helping teams across the organization analyze data, build tools, and move ideas into production. Alongside its Codex rollout, it is using the OpenAI API to develop more personalized member experiences, including through its AI Trainer.

For Santhosh Kumar, CTO at cult.fit, AI presented an opportunity to change how the organization works. “We wanted to become more AI-native in the way we run things,” he says. “How can we run our operations or transform our operations to be AI-first? What new customer experiences can we offer? And how can we transform how we run our organization?”

highlights.title: Nottingham Forest’s historic goal drought at home is part of longstanding problem
highlights.summary: Oliver Glasner’s side are yet to score at City Ground this season but troubles in front of goal precede his arrival. Nottingham Forest and Schalke are yet to score at home in 2026-27.
body: They also failed to find the net in a Carabao Cup home game with Leeds, meaning they have amassed 70 shots in all competitions without giving the home fans a goal to celebrate. As extreme as this situation has become, Forest scored only two goals more than the lowest home scorers in the Premier League last season (Burnley), drawing a blank on nine occasions. This is a longstanding issue.

The dishonour of scoring the fewest home goals in Europe’s big five leagues in modern times belongs to Dijon, who bagged eight in 19 Ligue 1 games in 2020-21. Fulham went one goal better in the same season to claim the Premier League’s wooden spoon for home scoring. Both scored three across their first four games, showing the unlikely depths to which Forest’s attack has sunk at the City Ground.

With expected goals a frequent element of post-match analysis, it can be easy to overlook that shots are independent of each other. One is not more likely to be converted when those that preceded it were missed, even though the team’s xG total ticks upward. A side that produced one expected goal through 100 shots valued at 0.01 xG would be far from guaranteed to score.

highlights.title: After gobbling up EA, Saudi Arabia and private equity firm Silver Lake reportedly looking to buy Unity
highlights.summary: After acquiring EA for $55bn earlier this year, Saudi Arabia and private equity firm Silver Lake are reportedly in the market for another massive video game company. And according to new reports, it's Unity.
body: Per Reuters, Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF) and Silver Lake - two major actors in the EA acquisition - are in talks to acquire the video game engine company for around $25bn. Silver Lake's Egon Durban already sits on the Unity Board of Directors, and the firm owns around eight percent of its shares already thanks to a $400m investment.

This $25bn valuation should be taken with a grain of salt for two core reasons. For one, it was decided prior to Unity's latest quarterly financial report, which included a 59% increase in strategic revenue year-over-year and net income of $122m. So this could propel the valuation upwards.

On the other hand, wider economic changes could have a detrimental effect. Reuters points out: "Strong ⁠growth in Unity's AI-powered Vector advertising platform helped it post its first quarterly profit on a GAAP basis since going public in September 2020." Given we've seen the generative AI sector take a major hit this week following the US midterm elections, it's possible companies using the tech may be viewed with more fiscal skepticism. Or, maybe this dip is just temporary. In short, take the $25bn valuation as a ballpark figure.

highlights.summary: Kärt Väinola, the head of the Just Film Industry Days, taking place during the Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival, also previews how AI and labels will be debated during its fourth edition.
body: Estonia’s Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival ( PÖFF ) kicks off its 30th anniversary edition on Friday. In addition to latest art house discoveries, movies for younger audiences will also take the spotlight at the event – as has become tradition.

PÖFF launched its popular Just Film Festival for youth and children’s movies in 2001. Since 2023, it has also organized the Just Film Industry Days to provide networking, education and pitching opportunities for people working in or looking at the space.

Kärt Väinola is the head of Just Film Industry Days, along with serving as Baltic Event Co-Production and International Works in Progress co-manager, Just Film Works in Progress manager and panels & talks coordinator.

She talked to THR about why Tallinn has been proudly putting the spotlight on kids and youth content, how it fits into broader industry trends and why social media bans, whether launched and considered, will be among the hot topics of discussion this year.
